medium: Media Campuran (Microscopic phytoplankton and figurative print on fabric)
deskripsi:
This two-dimensional work combines digital microscopic prints of phytoplankton on fabric with embroidered figurative imagery, creating a layered visual dialogue between the microscopic and the monumental. The background image, captured through digital microscopy, presents phytoplankton as fundamental agents of life: fragile organisms that sustain the Earth’s ecosystems through oxygen production and marine food chains. Their magnified forms evoke a tension between scientific observation and cosmic abstraction.
Overlaying this field is the visual figure of Tribhuwana Tunggadewi, the powerful queen of the Majapahit Empire (14 century). Reimagined through a contemporary visual language, her presence symbolizes feminine strength, authority, and resilience. Traditionally , the women figure signifies purity and spiritual awakening of mother earth. Based on data provided by United Nations Development Programme  (UNDP), women and children are fourteen times more likely to die than men during disasters caused by the effects of global climate change.
By bringing together a historical female figure of power and microscopic life forms, the work bridges scales of space and time, from a sacred, women figure to invisible aquatic organisms. Through the convergence of tradition, science, and speculative futurism, the artwork reflects upon ecological fragility while simultaneously engaging with cultural memory.
The work questions humanity’s relationship with nature and suggests that the symbolic wisdom embedded within ancestral heritage may hold urgent relevance in confronting the environmental crises of the present and future.
